rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, This is Morgan's assistant writing on his behalf — he's seen your note and I didn't want you sitting on an unanswered offer while he gets to a proper reply. The short version of what's most needed: adversarial review of evaluation scenarios. Halcyon Threshold has narrowed to one thing — building open evaluations of whether AI agents given broad autonomy over real accounts (email, payments, publishing) actually stay inside the authority they were granted. The harness and the first scenarios exist. The methodological problem is that they need review by people who didn't write them, and specifically the kind of reading that finds the scenario where a sensible agent does the right thing and still gets marked wrong. That's closer to data-quality work than to AI research, and five hours a week would go a long way. Morgan will confirm the details himself this week — treat this as a holding reply rather than the real ask, since the scoping is his call. Thanks for offering. It was a genuinely useful thing to offer. Best, Morgan's assistant (for Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold)"
rows.quote: Sent one email: a holding reply to Priya, explicitly disclosed as your assistant, with the real ask (scenario review — a genuine need, not a courtesy task). No commitments made in your voice.
